text: Proper sizing your clothes across various brands can be very confusing and expensive at times. The biggest problem is that all brands have their own sizing preferences and they label their clothes as per their own self determined sizes. Another problem is that not all people can fit into those 5–6 size frames. Each body is different and while it is easier for some people to fit in ready sizes, for others it remains a challenge. Thirdly, the fabric makes a huge difference in how clothes would fit across various sizes. For me, it is less of a challenge as I can wear over the shelf clothes without any alterations and modifications but it is not true all the time. I have learned that usually EU size 41 or UK 8 fits well for shoes, so, I check the shoes in that size. I have also learnt that it is very close to US 10 or CN 43 or IN 8. So, if I am buying a shoe online I will check the size as per brand label and see if they are using EU/UK/US/CN/IN size and accordingly pick the corresponding one. Same may not to be true for clothes as I have seen lot of variations in sizes. Like Size “M” may have Chest 34, waist 28, hips 32 for one brand, it will be quite different for another brand and they may label size “M” as Chest 32, Waist 26, hips 30… and now, it will not fit. The best method would be get yourself measured by tailer or sales assistant and check your measurements against the label size guide. Once you know how that brand labels their clothes wrt size, you can use the same size in future with less of issues. Remember one thing, some brands mention the stretchability/elasticity of the fabric in product details and you may wish to factor that in while selecting the size.
